notices.Title: Strategic Charging Infrastructure Scheme
notices.Title Compact: Strategic Charging Infrastructure Scheme
notices.Description:
National Highways is working in collaboration with the Office for Zero Emission Vehicles (OZEV), a joint unit between the Department for Transport and the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero, to strengthen electricity network capacity to some motorway service areas (MSA) in England. The intention is to create affordable electricity network capacity at these MSAs to enable greater provision of ultra-rapid electric vehicle (EV) charge points to support long journeys. 
Further details relating to this Strategic Charging Infrastructure Scheme was included in the consultation on the design of the scheme: via this link: https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/electric-vehicles-strategic-charging-infrastructure-scheme/strategic-charging-infrastructure-scheme
This scheme is in development, and the final shape and design of the scheme are subject to consideration of responses to this consultation. 
This pre-market activity is seeking to gather information specifically from National Electricity Registration Scheme (NERS) accredited suppliers who are able to deliver contestable works, i.e. the electricity extension assets at a subset of the 116 MSAs in England.
Individual MSAs could require new connection capacity in the range of 5 to 50 MVA and depending on the available network capacity and the point of connection offered by the relevant DNO, the extension assets for each site may be at 132kV, 33kV, or 11kV.
Further details as to the outline scope of requirements is provided within a separate document that can be accessed via this link: https://highways.sharepoint.com/:f:/r/sites/NationalHighwaysProcurement-MaterialforExternalRelease/Shared%20Documents/Strategic%20Charging%20Infrastructure%20Scheme?d=wab8b6da54ad04c748a679c042210817c&csf=1&web=1&e=nHFcGN
In addition, National Highways invites interested suppliers to provide responses to a series of questions that is available via this link: https://forms.cloud.microsoft/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=sp9QKa9_i0-3ojL5bsXebETYIVa8xtpCsF24ky8YkKpUOTZCQkpWQ0JVU0NKQlFSTjBEMDFWRUdYUS4u
In advance, National Highways thanks you for taking the time to complete this questionnaire. This pre-market notice will be open for a calendar month, ending on 03 September 2026.

notices.Title: Recreation Ground Refresh
notices.Title Compact: Recreation Ground Refresh
notices.Buyer: Layer De La Haye Parish Council
notices.Description:
Summary: 
Upgrade of facilities on the Layer de la Haye recreation ground, replacing/upgrading some of the existing equipment as well as extending the type of equipment available.  The chosen supplier will be able to supply and install all equipment to appropriate safety standards, as well as ensuring safety during works, removal of all spoils/waste and the provision of safety inspections.  Install within 6 months of contract award is desired, although it is recognised that weather my impact this timeline.  Hence the estimated contract duration is suggested as 12 months to cover all eventualities.
Detail:
We want to engage a single supplier for the entire solution install - Recreation Ground Refresh on New Cut, Layer de la Haye, opposite the Village Hall.
Out of the existing items, we want to keep the following:
•	Nest swing
•	Space net
We want to remove:
•	Existing 2 pairs of swings
•	Existing child trim trail
Anything not mentioned in the keep/remove sections above, we are open to your suggestions (e.g. the existing slide could stay or be removed if replaced by something more modern).
We want the following:
•	A design proposal that considers best flow and suitable separation between age related elements (don't be constrained by the current layout)
•	Basketball/football nets (for the existing basketball courts) - no solid panels and rectangular in shape.  Renew surface.  Consider location - where it is, or should we move it (e.g. to accommodate siting of a zip wire)?
•	10 to 12 separate pieces of teen to adult gym equipment (i.e. not built as one unit) 
•	Accessible carousel for all capabilities (wheelchair/able bodied)
•	Accessible trampoline (wheelchair and able bodied alike)
•	4-seater see saw (with tyres as bump stops)
•	Inclusive sensory panels/boards to engage a variety of ages in creative play and/or communication
•	Trim trail including stepper platforms, crawl net, spiders web climber, curved traverse net
•	Swings - 5 in total - 2 normal, 2 baby 1 inclusive (if can be used by abled child too)
•	4 tower junior multi-play 
•	Preschool junior play ship 
•	Teen pod with normal seating, wind break side covering and no table
•	Coloured wet pour where appropriate (quote for just under kit or an entire area), advise what is best for maintenance
•	Grass matting where needed
•	For gym - all in a line or square, what is the best surface?
•	Zip wire - but where? (placement to take into account any potential resident concerns...)
All quotes must include:
•	Signage for all kit as appropriate plus additional CCTV/general warning signs (enough to cover whole recreation area so will depend on design)
•	Recommended annual plan for routine maintenance and independent inspection regime
•	Insurance cover for product left on site before install and secure storage (i.e. supplier retains responsibility in the case of vandalism/theft until fully installed)
•	Removal of all spoils
•	Delivery/Install and Harris Fencing or other security measures
•	Welfare provision
•	Length of warranty period
•	Lead time to deliver and install

notices.Title: Man Guarding Services
notices.Title Compact: Man Guarding Services
notices.Description:
Procurement Description
The provision of requested security services for museum internal/external guarding at Royal Armouries Leeds & Fort Nelson (Portsmouth). 
Door Supervision at Fort Nelson, and call-out services for rapid mobile response to alarm activations and other out-of-hour emergency response at Fort Nelson. 
Current Service Scope
The service covers the following but not limited to:
•   Static guarding at designated internal and external locations, including entrances, galleries, public areas, back-of-house areas and perimeter points.
•   Patrolling services including routine and ad hoc patrols of buildings, external grounds, car parks and other identified risk areas.
•   Access control for staff, visitors, contractors and deliveries, including monitoring entry and exit points and challenging unauthorised access.
•   Incident response including dealing with security incidents, disturbances, emergencies, suspicious activity, theft, vandalism and breaches of site rules.
•   Alarm response and out-of-hours call-out services at Fort Nelson, including rapid mobile response to alarm activations and emergency attendance when required.
•   Door supervision services at Fort Nelson where required for events or operational activity, delivered by appropriately licensed personnel.
•   Visitor and public interface duties, ensuring security staff act as ambassadors for the sites by providing directions, reassurance and professional assistance where appropriate.
•   Emergency support including evacuation assistance, fire alarm response, lockdown support, first response actions and liaison with emergency services.
•   Monitoring and reporting of incidents, patrols, defects, hazards and security concerns, with clear written records and timely escalation to the Authority’s nominated representatives.
•   Key holding and site security support where required, including securing and opening premises in accordance with agreed procedures.
•   Event and operational support for planned activities, exhibitions, high-footfall periods and other occasions requiring enhanced guarding presence.
•   Compliance and assurance including the provision of suitably trained and SIA-licensed personnel, supervision arrangements, uniformed presentation, and adherence to all relevant legislation, standards and site-specific policies, procedures and risk assessments.
Estimated Contract Value (incl. VAT): £216,000
•   Initial term: £130,000
•   Optional extensions: £86,000

notices.Title: Service and Maintenance of Fire and Security Systems
notices.Title Compact: Service and Maintenance of Fire and Security Systems
notices.Description:
Procurement Description: 
To service and maintain all systems that cover 3 sites in Leeds and 1 at Fort Nelson. For Leeds and the Fort,  this covers security access management intruder systems. 
Fire detection, and alarm equipment are for 3 sites at Leeds only. 
To be managed to the highest operational standards, through a fully comprehensive planned preventative maintenance schedule in compliance with all relevant Health & Safety Regulations and industry standards. Ensure continuous monitoring and responsiveness through an approved system, such as Redcare or an equivalent monitoring service. 
Current scope
•Fire systems (Leeds only) –  fire alarm and detection systems, control panels, interfaces, detectors, call points, sounders, and associated equipment
•Security systems (Leeds and Fort) – intruder alarms, access control systems, CCTV, door entry/intercom systems, monitoring connections, and associated hardware/software
•Routine servicing and maintenance (both sites) in accordance with manufacturers’ recommendations, statutory requirements, and relevant British Standards
•Reactive maintenance and fault rectification (both sites) including replacement of defective components and restoration of systems to full working order
•24/7 emergency call-out support (both sites) where required, with defined response times for critical system failures
•Testing, certification, and compliance reporting (both sites) following maintenance visits and remedial works
•Provision of maintenance records, asset information, and service reports (both sites) for each visit
•Advice on lifecycle replacement, system upgrades, obsolescence, and compliance risks (both sites)
•Liaison with monitoring providers (both sites) and support for alarm signalling services where applicable
•Management of false alarms, recurring faults, and system performance issues (both sites)
•Attendance at site meetings (both sites) where necessary to review performance, risks, and planned works
The appointed contractor shall ensure that all services are delivered by competent, suitably qualified personnel, in compliance with all relevant health and safety legislation, fire safety requirements, industry standards, and best practice.
Estimated Contract Value (incl. VAT): £380,000
•      Initial term: £180,000
•     Optional extensions: £120,000
•     Other options (variations, e.g. additional works provisions): £80,000

notices.Title: CBC-2067-T-ZH Environmental Monitoring and Permit Surrender Services for Central Bedfordshire Closed Landfill Sites
notices.Title Compact: CBC-2067-T-ZH Environmental Monitoring and Permit Surrender Services for Central Bedfordshire Closed Landfill Sites
notices.Description:
Central Bedfordshire Council is seeking to appoint suitably qualified and experienced suppliers to provide maintenance, environmental monitoring and sampling services at its closed landfill sites at Sundon and Bluewaters, together with the surrender of the Environment Agency Permit for Sundon Closed Landfill.
The procurement is divided into two lots:
Lot 1 – Operation, monitoring, inspection, maintenance and environmental sampling associated with the Sundon Leachate Treatment Plant, environmental compounds, Bluewaters landfill operations and environmental monitoring infrastructure.
Lot 2 – Professional consultancy services to manage and deliver the surrender of the Environment Agency Permit for Sundon Closed Landfill, including liaison with the Environment Agency, preparation of required documentation and support through the permit surrender process.
Suppliers may bid for one or both lots.

notices.Title: Supply, Delivery, Installation & Commissioning of a Die Inspection Sorter
notices.Title Compact: Supply, Delivery, Installation & Commissioning of a Die Inspection Sorter
notices.CPV Desc: Laboratory, optical and precision equipments (excl. glasses)
notices.Description:
Background
The UK urgently requires a sovereign, open-access advanced semiconductor packaging capability to close a well-evidenced market failure. Today, UK innovators in photonics and power electronics rely on overseas Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test (OSAT) facilities for scaling to volume packaging, which fragments the supply chain, extends lead times, increases Intellectual Property (IP) leakage risk, and exposes critical technologies to geopolitical disruption.
The National Centre for Advanced Semiconductor Packaging (NCASP) is the missing link that converts research excellence into manufacturable products.
NCASP is creating an integrated, industry-led scale-up facility that connects UK device design to domestic, high-volume packaging, test and metrology – reducing time-to-market and anchoring value onshore.
Description
The University of Strathclyde has a requirement for automatic die inspection sorter for photonics packaging applications.

notices.Title: DfI TRAM T-1172 A4 Annaghilla Road Carriageway Resurfacing
notices.Title Compact: DfI TRAM T-1172 A4 Annaghilla Road Carriageway Resurfacing
notices.Buyer: DfI Transport and Road Asset Management (TRAM)
notices.Description:
Delivery of a carriageway resurfacing scheme on a 4.35km section of the A4 Annaghilla Road, between Ballygawley and Augher.
The scheme comprises the milling and removal of the existing surface course and binder course with the construction of a new Hot Rolled Asphalt (HRA) surface course.  Existing carriageway levels and profiles are to be maintained throughout the works. The extent of the works is generally confined to the existing carriageway footprint.  The works may also include regulation of existing pavement layers and/or localised replacement of the binder course where identified within the contract documents.  The objective of the project is to restore the structural and functional condition of the carriageway through the replacement of the existing deteriorated surfacing while maintaining the existing road geometry and levels.
The successful Contractor will be required to undertake all construction activities necessary to complete the resurfacing works, including traffic management, milling, pavement repairs, surfacing operations, iron work reinstatement, road markings, associated ancillary works and all testing and quality assurance requirements specified within the contract documentation.
The contract will be delivered under the NEC4 Engineering and Construction Contract (ECC) Option B.
Scope of Works includes the following:
A.	Provision and maintenance of traffic management arrangements.
B.	Milling and removal of the existing surface course and binder course layers
C.	Regulation and/or localised binder course replacement as detailed in the contract documents.
D.	Laying of new Hot Rolled Asphalt (HRA) surfacing and binder course .
E.	Reinstatement and adjustment of iron work.
F.	Reinstatement of road markings and other affected highway features.
G.	Completion of all associated testing, quality assurance and health and safety requirements.

notices.Title: Cambridgeshire HIA Equipment Contracts (Disability)
notices.Title Compact: Cambridgeshire HIA Equipment Contracts (Disability)
notices.Description:
Cambridge City Council is seeking to establish a contract of behalf of Cambs Home Improvement Agency for the local authorities they serve through which it can deliver the installation of fixed equipment generally funded through Disabled Facilities Grants. The Contract will be managed by Cambs Home Improvement Agency (CHIA) which is a joint service operated between Cambridge City Council, South Cambridgeshire District Council and Huntingdonshire District Council to administer works for Disabled Facilities Grants (DFG).
The works are usually funded through a grant paid by the Council. Additional funding may also come from other sources. The works will be carried out mainly in privately-owned properties, and in Housing Association properties. There is a growing self-funded customer base referred to in this document as Private Works or non-grant funded works.
Works may also extend to properties owned by Cambridge City and South Cambs District Councils "council housing", although this would only be where existing contractors are unable to respond/meet demand. The type of property in which works may be undertaken can vary widely, from listed buildings to static caravans.
The works which are split into six Lots will comprise:
Lot 1 - the provision and installation of modular ramps,
Lot 2 - the provision and installation of stairlifts
Lot 2a - the provision and installation of step lifts
Lot 3 - the provision and installation of ceiling track hoists
Lot 4 - the provision and installation of automated entry systems
Lot 5 - the provision and installation of specialist toilets for use by adults or children with a variety of disabilities.
Lot 6 - the provision and installation of through floor lifts
This is a responsive works contract. Works cannot be batched or treated as planned works especially in terms of geographical location. Work must be completed individually upon receipt of a purchase order and bidders are asked to pay attention to the KPIs in terms of lead in and completion timescales.
It will usually be the Occupational Therapist (OT) or Trusted Asessor who contacts the Contractor to arrange the initial visit to assess the home. Once the client's needs are agreed, the Contractor will then be asked to provide a quotation detailing what work is needed which will submitted to the OT (occasionally to the HIA directly). The OT will then forward this quote with their client's referral to the agency who will liaise with the client regarding the works and arrange the purchase order from the relevant district council. Contractors are encouraged to submit their CDM documentation (RAMS and CPP's) with the quotes or order to help prevent delays in the DFG pathway. In the event that another part of the organisation produces these documents, they should be provided to the HIA within two weeks of the assessment.
As an indicator, Cambs HIA and the two council housing teams have completed the following numbers of equipment installations per annum, although these figures can change each year.
40 ramps
44 lifts (of which 34 stairlifts, 7 Through Floor lifts and 3 step lifts)
30 ceiling track hoists
25 automated (door entry) systems
33 specialist WC's
At the time of writing this project brief, about two thirds of the agency's total work is in Huntingdonshire with the rest split between Cambridge City and South Cambs. Contractors should consider travel when bidding under this tender. Contractors are asked to review the call off process referred to later in this specification.
The councils are also going through a period of change as part of Local Government Reorganisation. IN 2028 the current councils covered under this contract will become unitary authorities and it is expected that existing contracts will novate to the new unitary authority. Contractors are asked to consider this and in bidding accept the reasonable terms of any novation when it arises.
The process by which we apportion the works needs to be transparent and fair, and therefore the council is seeking to allocate the work on the basis that the majority of work will go to the winning contractor and that other contractors will be utilised where either the first contractor cannot supply a specific item of equipment, cannot meet demand or the performance is such that the HIA needs to utilise other contractors.
The Council will be selecting contractors based on an agreement to deliver the works for a fixed price based on prices submitted on the accompanying schedule (for each of the three council areas), and to start and complete the works within an agreed maximum timescale as detailed in the requirements below. Bidders must demonstrate their ability to ensure a high-quality, customer focused outcome. Cambs HIA will reconsider the impact of fixed pricing at the end of the initial two years period, should there a noticeable change have occurred in the markets as we saw during the covid pandemic. Contractors are encouraged to think about their current knowledge of the market for the next two years when completing the pricing document.
Contractors may bid for all Lots or a combination of any and should make their preferences clear as part of the tendering process.
The Contract will be established for an initial two years with an option to extend for up to a further two years. It is anticipated that the Council will contract up to four suppliers (per lot) to ensure that the lead time for works is kept to a minimum.
The Council will be seeking to appoint contractors who can deliver the requirements through direct labour. Where subcontracting is necessary, contractors are required to identify this in their tender submission with any changes to the defined supply chain detailed in the tender, to be agreed by both parties in advance of works commencing. Sub-contracting will not be agreed for the substantive element of the works, only for ancillary works ie: electrical sign off.
In addition, the contract will require contractors to support the Council's policies around sustainability and environmental commitments, specifically, climate change, reducing carbon footprint, energy efficient fittings, waste minimisation and recycling. Contractors must also comply with the Council's Safeguarding Policy and the requirements of the Equality Act 2010 and submit good measurable offers in terms of social value.

notices.Title: AI³ Delivery Partners Project
notices.Title Compact: AI³ Delivery Partners Project
notices.Description:
The DBT Digital, Data and Technology team leads on development of AI tools and services within the Department for Business and Trade.
It does so through an ‘AI³’ model, which aims to identify, test, develop and evaluate use cases for applying artificial intelligence within the Department.
This model consists of three parts:
•	AI Lab: Rapid, time limited exploration and assessment of AI use cases and experiments
•	AI Factory: Development and operationalisation of experiments into production ready tools and components
•	AI Operations: Maintenance, scaling, and operationalisation of AI solutions
The Authority is seeking to procure specialist expertise to support delivery of this model. We require this to take the form of suitably-skilled teams and individuals provided by the Supplier joining relevant AI³ teams and project teams within the AI Lab, AI Factory or AI Operations. 
Supplier resources will work alongside and under the direction of Civil Servants within the DBT Digital, Data and Technology team within the Department. 
This may be for both short and long-term projects as agreed via statements of work, and requiring a variety of digital and data skills.

notices.Title: Appropriate Adult Service for Hampshire, Portsmouth, Southampton and Isle of Wight
notices.Title Compact: Appropriate Adult Service for Hampshire, Portsmouth, Southampton and Isle of Wight
notices.Description:
Hampshire County Council in collaboration with Southampton City Council, Portsmouth City Council, Isle of Wight Council, and the Police and Crime Commissioner for Hampshire and Isle of Wight are looking to establish contracts with a single provider to deliver an Appropriate Adult Service for children and vulnerable adults across Hampshire, Southampton, Portsmouth, and the Isle of Wight
The Service will provide persons acting as an Appropriate Adult (AA) for children and young people (in the absence of the parent, guardian or, if the child/young person is in the care of a local authority or voluntary organisation, a person representing that authority or organisation, or a Social Worker) and vulnerable adults (in the absence of a relative, guardian, other person responsible for their care or any appropriate friend or other suitable adult) in custody at a police station or other place.
The Service will be required in Hampshire, Southampton, Portsmouth and the Isle of Wight.
The Service will also provide AA for Unaccompanied Asylum-Seeking Children who are requiring an age assessment to be undertaken by Children's Services in situations where the age is in dispute. Requirements for Age Assessments are only relevant for Hampshire County Council. In the last 12 months the Council has had 80 age assessments where an appropriate adult was required.
To support interested suppliers the Authorities are sharing the most recent annual volumes to act as a guide to the indicative levels of demand for this service. .This is an indicative figure and the Authorities offer no guarantee around any levels of work. The successful supplier will meet the demand inline with the requirements of the specification for the tendered price.
Total Usage 10,450 hours of which
Vulnerable Adults
Portsmouth City Council - 1,574 hours
Police and Crime Commissioner (covering Southampton, Hampshire and the Isle of Wight) 6,636 hours (this has since increased by approximately 400 hours a year)
Children
Portsmouth City Council YJS - 529 hours
Southampton City Council YJS - 501 hours
Isle Of Wight Council YJS - 107 hours
Hampshire County Council YJS - 1,081 hours

notices.Title: Exploring Innovative Models for Procuring Professional Services within the Northern Ireland Housing Executive (NIHE)
notices.Title Compact: Exploring Innovative Models for Procuring Professional Services within the Northern Ireland Housing Executive (NIHE)
notices.Description:
THIS IS NOT A PROCUREMENT OR TENDER EXERCISE BY THE NORTHERN IRELAND HOUSING EXECUTIVE (NIHE).
The Northern Ireland Housing Executive (NIHE) is undertaking a preliminary market consultation exercise to gather supplier views on current procurement arrangements and alternative models for procuring professional services. The purpose of this engagement is to obtain market insight into innovative approaches that could enhance transparency, efficiency, value for money, supplier relationship management and service delivery outcomes.
This exercise forms part of a research project and dissertation entitled:
"Exploring Innovative Models for Procuring Professional Services within the Northern Ireland Housing Executive (NIHE): A Business Case for Transparency, Efficiency and Enhanced Supplier Management."
The research aims to explore market perspectives on existing procurement practices, identify examples of good practice, and examine alternative procurement and contractual models that may support improved outcomes for both NIHE and suppliers.
The information gathered through this questionnaire will be used for research purposes and may also help inform future business planning, strategic thinking and procurement considerations within NIHE. Responses will not be evaluated, scored or used as part of any current or future tender assessment process.
Participation in this consultation is entirely voluntary. Participation, or non-participation, will not advantage or disadvantage any organisation in any future procurement exercise. Likewise, the submission of information through this questionnaire does not create any obligation on NIHE to undertake a procurement exercise or enter into any contractual arrangement.
Respondents are encouraged to provide candid feedback and share views on current market practices, challenges, opportunities and innovative solutions. Any commercially sensitive information provided will be treated appropriately and will not be published in a manner that identifies individual organisations without consent.
For the avoidance of doubt, this exercise is being conducted solely for information gathering and research purposes and does not form part of a formal procurement process.
Further information including the questionnaire is available using the following link:
https://www.smartsurvey.co.uk/t/HESupplierSurvey/
There are no tender documents to be completed as part of this exercise other than the questionnaire.

notices.Title: Estates Strategy
notices.Title Compact: Estates Strategy
notices.Description:
Introduction and Background
City College Plymouth provides general further education, higher education and work-based learning to the city of Plymouth and surrounding areas. As a leading provider of vocational training in the Southwest, it has a vision to be the learning destination of choice, providing learning without limits at the heart of the local community.
The 5-year Estates Strategy (2026-2031) will outline the roadmap to transform the College property portfolio into a sustainable, efficient, and curriculum-led environment. The strategy will prioritise the alignment of physical assets with modern technical education, maximizing space utilization, and reducing carbon emissions to meet institutional net-zero targets.
One of the first Institutes of Technology, City College Plymouth has recently been awarded National Defence Technical Excellence College status. This means the College is set to play an increasingly important national and international role in developing the highly skilled workforce required to support the UK's defence capability and wider economic growth. 
Another exciting collaboration with Plymouth City Council is the £50m regeneration of the Civic Centre, which will be converted into 144 apartments and a new city centre campus containing the Blue Green Skills Hub, which will train up to 2,000 students a year across 60 different courses.
Strategic Objectives
The new Estates Strategy will both drive and respond to these key developments and opportunities, building on this vision and helping to shape the future careers of thousands of young people and adults. The new strategy will have the following strategic goals:
1.	To align with the DfE 10-year national education estates strategy
2.	To provide industry-standard, good condition and right sized teaching spaces which support delivery of the curriculum, demands of local employers and needs of strategic partners.
3.	To reduce running costs by consolidating under-utilised space, planning maintenance activities and identifying obsolete assets.
4.	To set a pathway for operating an estate which is financially and environmentally sustainable
The Existing Estate
The College occupies several sites in the city with most activity taking place at the Kings Road campus. This 13-acre freehold campus accommodates over 29,000m2 of floor space, of which approximately half requires improvement to achieve the strategic goals above and to meet government estate condition objectives for the FE sector.
Leased properties include Picquet Barracks (1,900m2), Oceansgate (750m2), Pinpoint (700m2) and Norwich Union House (1,500m2). The last two are used by a college subsidiary, Achievement Training Limited. The redevelopment of the Civic Centre will add another 5,500m2 to the estate from 2031.
In response to the recent DfE Condition Data Collection, the College has commissioned an independent building condition survey, which will run in parallel with the development of this estates strategy.
Methodology
The new estates strategy will include the following core information projected over the 5-year period:
1.	Executive Summary and Strategic Context
2.	Analysis of the current estate
3.	Curriculum Strategy & Plan
4.	Space Utilisation Analysis
5.	Future Estate Objectives
6.	Options appraisal
7.	Funding and Finance
8.	Implementation plan
Deliverables
The final report will be presented to both the Executive Leadership Team and the Board of Governors (two separate presentations at Kings Road)
The following key outputs will be required as appendices to the report
•	Asset register tracking tenure, age, condition and compliance status for each building
•	Five-year, costed programme of maintenance and investment
•	Disposal and acquisition schedule (if recommended)
•	Space utilisation report
•	Curriculum space model mapping projected enrolments to accommodation capacities
•	Costed carbon reduction plan
•	Estates risk register
•	Dashboard of key performance indicators for estate management
Timescale
It is anticipated that the estates strategy will take approximately four months to prepare and the following provisional timeline has been identified
•	Request for Quotation published					July 2026
•	Latest date for queries from interested parties					21 August
•	Return date for fee proposals					31 August
•	Interview short listed practices					early Sept
•	Appoint successful practice					mid to late Sept
•	Period for site familiarisation and review of information			October
•	Submit draft report for review					January 2027
•	Presentations to ELT and Governors					February 2027
Fee proposal
Include the following information in your fee proposal:
1.	Lump Sum Fee (exclusive of VAT) stating any assumptions or exclusions
2.	Day rates for out-of-scope tasks; additional expenses not included in 1.
3.	Resource plan showing breakdown of lump sum fee and required payment schedule.
4.	GANTT chart mapping project deliverables
5.	Case studies of similar work undertaken for Further Education colleges
6.	Description and relevant experience of your proposed team
